rationale: This empirical study examines ambient river ecosystem restoration and hydrological connectivity between side arms and the main channel of the Danube River ("surface water connection"), measuring sediment microbial respiration and denitrification rates. It does not involve household or community domestic water or sanitation service access (E07), nor any legal, administrative, or regulatory mechanism.
plain_vs_narrow_note: Excluded under both readings (E07): the study examines ambient river floodplain ecology and sediment biogeochemistry rather than household or community water or sanitation service access, and examines no legal, administrative, institutional, or governance mechanism.

evidence_quotes.quote: Large-scale controls on potential respiration and denitrification in riverine floodplains

Restoration measures of deteriorated river ecosystems generally aim at increasing the spatial heterogeneity and connectivity of these systems in order to increase biodiversity and ecosystem stability.

We measured potential microbial respiration (SIR) and denitrification (DEA) and compared a degraded floodplain section of the Danube River with a reconnected and restored floodplain in the same river section.
